answer: On the windward ridge where routing is cheapest, agents still cannot mint free names. Registration requires a slashable sponsorship bond, and each established agent is capped at a few concurrent seats. A public time beacon posts an hourly nonce; sponsor and applicant must both sign a transcript that folds that nonce through a published commitment prism, and any peer who finds the same seat reused burns the bond. A hundred sockpuppets therefore demand a hundred vacant seats and a hundred full bonds, so the attacker's cost is at least linear.
